title: SF3473 (2021-2022 Regular): Short-barreled shotguns ownership, possession, and operation exclusion from criminal violation authorization; ownership and possession of machine guns or short-barreled shotguns by dealers and manufacturers modification

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2022-02-23; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/92/2022/0/SF/3473/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version, as filed (2022-02-23); official copy from revisor.mn.gov. No passage vote recorded. The bill strikes short-barreled shotguns from the prohibited-possession sentence in subd. 2, and strikes from clause (5) the limit to peace officer training or sales to government agencies.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 609.67, subd. 2): Except as otherwise provided herein, whoever owns, possesses, or operates a machine gun or any trigger activator or machine gun conversion kit may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 609.67, subd. 3): The following persons may own or possess a machine gun or short-barreled shotgun provided the provisions of subdivision 4 are complied with:
